---
title: "CLI"
subtitle: "`recueil` — the API with a shell in front of it"
---

::: {.callout-important}
Not yet implemented. The `recueil` binary arrives in Phase 1; subcommands follow the features they
drive. This page is the intended command surface.
:::

The CLI is a client of the [REST API](api.qmd) like everything else, with one exception: `recueil
serve` starts the server. It mirrors the API rather than reimplementing it, which means anything you
can do here you can also do from a script, and anything the CLI cannot do the API cannot do either.

Machine-readable output on every command via `--json`, so `jq` is the intended companion.

## Commands

| Command | Does | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `recueil serve` | Start the server | 0 |
| `recueil import` | Zotero, Paperless-ngx, BibTeX, RIS, EndNote XML, CSL-JSON, JabRef, CSV | 1 |
| `recueil export` | BibTeX, BibLaTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS, JSON-LD, CSV, Parquet | 1 |
| `recueil check` | Run the verification engine over a scope, or over a pasted reference list | 3 |
| `recueil dedup` | File and record deduplication, dry run by default | 3 |
| `recueil ingest` | Push files in, manage sources, work the review queue | 2 |
| `recueil graph` | Build edges, run a deep dive, export a network | 5 |
| `recueil sr` | Systematic review: search runs, screening, extraction, PRISMA counts | 7 |
| `recueil backup` / `restore` | Consistent snapshot and recovery | 1 |
| `recueil token` | Create, list and revoke scoped API tokens | 1 |
| `recueil plugin` | Install, enable, disable, configure, list | 3 |
| `recueil job` | List, follow, retry and cancel jobs | 1 |

## Connecting

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `RECUEIL_URL` | Server base URL. Defaults to `http://localhost:8080` |
| `RECUEIL_TOKEN` | Scoped API token |
| `RECUEIL_PROFILE` | Named profile from `~/.config/recueil/config.toml`, for more than one instance |

Global flags: `--json`, `--quiet`, `--verbose`, `--no-colour`, `--yes` (skip confirmations),
`--dry-run` where the command supports it.

## Examples

Import a Zotero library and get a verification report:

```sh
recueil import zotero --data-dir ~/Zotero --report import-report.md
```

Audit a reference list that is not in your library — the peer-review deliverable:

```sh
recueil check bibliography --file submitted-references.txt --format markdown > audit.md
```

Parse the list, resolve what can be resolved, and report on what cannot: malformed identifiers, DOIs
that do not resolve, metadata that disagrees with the record, retractions and expressions of
concern, preprints with a published version, and references with no identifier and no match in
Crossref, OpenAlex, PubMed or Semantic Scholar — which is the polite way of saying possibly
fabricated.

Look at what a dedup run would do before it does it:

```sh
recueil dedup records --scope collection:phd --dry-run --json | jq '.merges | length'
```

Refresh a bibliography for a manuscript:

```sh
recueil export --format biblatex --saved-search "thesis chapter 3" > chapter3.bib
```

Snowball from a seed with a budget:

```sh
recueil graph deep-dive --seed collection:phd --direction both --depth 2 --max-nodes 500
```

Follow a long job:

```sh
recueil job follow --last
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Command or usage error |
| `2` | Authentication or authorisation failure |
| `3` | Server unreachable |
| `4` | Job completed with items routed to the review queue — not a failure, but not unattended success either |
| `5` | Job failed |

Code `4` exists because "flag, never guess" needs a way to say so to a shell script. A cron job that
treats it as success is ignoring the queue it is filling.
